kernels.l1: In a full machine, every cubby gets used. Nothing is left empty.
kernels.l2: A machine fills up the second list when every thing on that list has at least one arrow landing on it. Change the second list and the answer changes.
kernels.l3: A function is onto when every element of the codomain is actually hit — the image is the whole codomain. Whether a function is onto depends on which codomain you declared.
kernels.l4: A function is onto when every element of the declared target is actually attained. That makes it a statement about the target, so the same rule can be onto or not depending on what you declared it to be.
kernels.l5: Surjectivity means every element of the codomain has a pre-image; it is a property of the pair (rule, codomain), not of the rule alone.
kernels.l6: A function is surjective when every element of the codomain is reached by something. The property depends on the codomain you declared and not on the rule alone — shrink the codomain to the image and any function becomes surjective.
kernels.l7: f is surjective when its image equals its codomain, so every target has at least one pre-image. The property depends on the declared codomain and not on the rule alone.
kernels.l8: Surjections are the epimorphisms of Set; the existence of a right inverse for every surjection is equivalent to the Axiom of Choice.
